content: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. In a deluge of nearly identical press releases, the various AGs accuse the company of planning to auction off "the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts - more than 2.1 million of them registered to minors - with no safeguards for the people whose conversations are being sold." In October, Character.AI filed for bankruptcy following years of scandals and legal challenges , including from Disney . content: A couple of Walmart's budget-friendly smart home cameras will be able to recognize people around your house now using Google's familiar face detection feature. A new Google Home update brings Familiar Faces support to the $35 Onn Outdoor Camera Plug-In and $77 Onn Floodlight Camera Hardwired. However, a Google Home Premium subscription is still required to access the feature. Both cameras and Google's Nest Cam Outdoor (wired, 2nd gen) also have a new remote control in the Google Home app you can use to start or stop a 30-second security siren while watching the camera's live video feed.
